summary: A lower pane comparing each bar's volume with its range, flagging high-effort, low-result bars and the reverse.
overview: Effort vs Result compares how much traded with how far price moved. Effort is the bar's volume against its average; result is the bar's range against its average. Both are drawn in their own pane.
Bars with high effort and low result are flagged in amber. Bars with low effort and high result are flagged in violet.
how: Averages run over 20 bars. A bar is flagged as high effort, low result when its effort is at least 1.5 times average and its effort-to-result ratio is at least 2. The reverse flag marks bars that moved far on little volume; it can be turned off.
It uses traded volume where order flow exists and the chart's own volume elsewhere.
use: Some traders read high effort with little movement as one side meeting the other.
Use the low effort flags to see moves that came on thin volume.
Some traders compare the flags with nearby support or resistance.
notes: It compares bars with their own recent average, so the same volume can flag differently on different days.
